title: bug: a candidate-edited package-lock.json still sends the check's offline npm ci to candidate bytes through entries host admission skips (lock root specs, root-level inBundle)
description: dependency-cache.mjs admission skips packages[''] and every inBundle entry. The guest preflight (task-5ed445ca) only compares package.json with the workspace lock root and never compares the lock with the bytes admission saw. Repro (npm 11.19.1, guest-supervisor.py 83a1f964, real run_install): (1) lock root and package.json both declare dependencies {a: 'file:stub/a-1.0.0.tgz'}, while node_modules/a stays a cached registry entry; (2) unchanged root, plus node_modules/a = {version '1.0.0', resolved 'file:stub/a-1.0.0.tgz', integrity of the stub, inBundle: true}. Both pass buildDependencyCache and the preflight, and npm ci installs the stub's stub.txt (status 42). Scratch: /tmp/moe-5ed-red8.giHYXx/kir.test.mjs (KIR). The route needs a candidate that can change package-lock.json. CQ-R11e3a treats lockfiles as untrusted, but task-5ed445ca's plan assumed the admitted lockfile is protected.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Host lockfile admission (admitLockfiles, so buildDependencyCache before any fetch or cache write) refuses every candidate package-lock.json shape that makes the pinned npm's offline `npm ci` install bytes other than the admitted registry tarballs. That covers a non-registry spec in any entry's dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies or peerDependencies (the root included), a bundled (inBundle) entry that names its own resolved or legacy _resolved, and a truthy hasShrinkwrap or _hasShrinkwrap. Each refusal is the fixed DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED; a non-object root is DEPENDENCY_LOCKFILE_INVALID. Every lockfile admitted today that has none of these shapes is admitted exactly as before, with the same dirs and packages.
acceptanceCriteria: Both filed routes refuse with DEPENDENCY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED before any fetch or cache write: a lock root (with a matching package.json) naming a file: spec, and a root-level inBundle entry with a file: resolved. So do the further proven routes: root devDependencies; entry dependencies, optionalDependencies and peerDependencies specs; nested or hoisted bundled entries with resolved or _resolved; and hasShrinkwrap/_hasShrinkwrap truthy. The refusal text never echoes a spec, dir or path (DA6, DA8).

Every registry spec form npm writes stays admitted with an unchanged package set: version, range, x-range, hyphen and || ranges, v/= prefixes, prerelease/build, tag, '', '*', and npm: aliases including scoped ones. So do bundled entries with no resolved/_resolved (still skipped, never fetched) and falsy shrinkwrap flags (DA7).
Under the host npm's own npm-package-arg, every spec admission accepts is a registry spec or one npm refuses, over fixed lists and a seeded 4000-spec spread (DA9).
With the real pinned npm, a registry tarball that bundles its dependency installs offline from the admitted tree through the supervisor's run_install (DA10).
